Predictive States — F1 / F2 Analysis¶

Working notebook for the "predictive states" blog post: which states have the longest track record of voting with the National Popular Vote (NPV) winner and/or the Electoral College (EC) winner, and how that's changed over time.

Two formalizations are used throughout (see docs/predictive-states-methodology on the blog for the full derivation):

  • F1 — longest streak tolerating k misses. For a given tolerance k, the longest contiguous run of elections with at most k misses. Used for display — it's the intuitive "27 of 28" framing.
  • F2 — baseline-centered maximum-subarray score. Each election scores (1 - p) on a match and -p on a miss, where p is the (possibly time-varying) baseline hit rate that election year; the best-scoring contiguous window is found via a Kadane's-algorithm-style scan (this is a CUSUM / change-point statistic). Used for selecting/ranking which states are worth featuring, since it self-tunes its own miss tolerance and isn't dominated by short lucky streaks the way a bare "% correct" would be.

Run all cells top-to-bottom once, then each state section below is independent and can be re-run / exported on its own — cells are tagged with the state's postal code plus its narrative category (see index below) so you can filter by tag when exporting individual sections.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

# Set to False if you want light-background plots (e.g. to match a light blog theme).
DARK_MODE = True
if DARK_MODE:
    plt.style.use("dark_background")

ACCENT = "#4FC3F7"
HIGHLIGHT = "#FFB300"
MISS_COLOR = "#EF5350"

DATA_DIR = "data"   # expects results_1789_2024.csv and presidential_margins.csv here
In [2]:
results = pd.read_csv(f"{DATA_DIR}/results_1789_2024.csv")
margins = pd.read_csv(f"{DATA_DIR}/presidential_margins.csv")

# collapse to (year, state, unit) grain -- unit==state drops congressional-district
# splits (ME/NE post-2008, and the historical KY/MD/NC/TN/NY district splits).
# Change this filter if you want to analyze districts as their own units instead.
_grp = results.groupby(["year", "state", "unit"], as_index=False).agg(
    matches_npv=("matches_npv", "first"),
    matches_ec=("matches_ec", "first"),
)
statelevel = _grp[_grp.unit == _grp.state].copy()

# state's own popular-vote winner (plurality of raw_votes) per (year, state)
_sl = results[results.state == results.unit].dropna(subset=["raw_votes"]).copy()
_idx = _sl.groupby(["year", "state"])["raw_votes"].idxmax()
state_winner = _sl.loc[_idx, ["year", "state", "candidate", "party"]].rename(
    columns={"candidate": "state_cand", "party": "state_party"}
)

METRIC_LABEL = {"matches_npv": "National Popular Vote", "matches_ec": "Electoral College"}

# baselines for F2: a single pooled constant, and a per-election-year rate
YEARLY_P = {m: statelevel.groupby("year")[m].mean().to_dict() for m in ["matches_npv", "matches_ec"]}
POOLED_P = {m: statelevel[m].dropna().mean() for m in ["matches_npv", "matches_ec"]}

print("Loaded:", len(results), "candidate-level rows /", len(statelevel), "state-year rows")
print("Pooled baseline hit rates:", {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in POOLED_P.items()})

# which years provide the highest/lowest hit rates for each metric
for m in ["matches_npv", "matches_ec"]:
    yearly = YEARLY_P[m]
    sorted_years = sorted(yearly.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Top years for {METRIC_LABEL[m]}:", sorted_years[:5])
    print(f"Bottom years for {METRIC_LABEL[m]}:", sorted_years[-5:])

Core functions: F1 and F2¶

In [3]:
def _valid_pairs(state, metric):
    """(year, bool) pairs for a state's valid (non-NaN) observations, sorted by year."""
    sub = statelevel[statelevel.state == state].sort_values("year")
    return [(y, bool(v)) for y, v in zip(sub.year, sub[metric]) if pd.notna(v)]


def longest_run_at_most_k_misses(bits, k):
    """F1: classic sliding-window / 'longest subarray with at most k zeros'. O(n)."""
    left = 0
    misses = 0
    best = 0
    for right, b in enumerate(bits):
        if not b:
            misses += 1
        while misses > k:
            if not bits[left]:
                misses -= 1
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best


def f1_curve(state, metric, kmax=3):
    """f_s(k) for k = 0..kmax -- the whole tolerance curve, not just one k."""
    bits = [b for _, b in _valid_pairs(state, metric)]
    return [longest_run_at_most_k_misses(bits, k) for k in range(kmax + 1)]
In [4]:
def max_subarray_score(pairs, p_of_year):
    """F2 core: Kadane's algorithm on the baseline-centered score.
    p_of_year: dict {year: p} for a time-varying baseline, or a float constant."""
    best, best_i, best_j = -1e9, 0, 0
    cur, cur_start = 0.0, 0
    for i, (y, b) in enumerate(pairs):
        p = p_of_year[y] if isinstance(p_of_year, dict) else p_of_year
        s = (1 - p) if b else -p
        if cur <= 0:
            cur, cur_start = s, i
        else:
            cur += s
        if cur > best:
            best, best_i, best_j = cur, cur_start, i
    return best, best_i, best_j


def f2_window(state, metric, baseline="time_varying"):
    """Returns the best-scoring window for (state, metric, baseline choice), or None."""
    pairs = _valid_pairs(state, metric)
    if len(pairs) < 3:
        return None
    p_of_year = YEARLY_P[metric] if baseline == "time_varying" else POOLED_P[metric]
    score, i, j = max_subarray_score(pairs, p_of_year)
    window = pairs[i : j + 1]
    length = len(window)
    hits = sum(1 for _, b in window if b)
    return dict(
        state=state, metric=metric, baseline=baseline,
        start=window[0][0], end=window[-1][0], length=length,
        hits=hits, misses=length - hits,
        miss_years=[y for y, b in window if not b],
        score=round(float(score), 2),
    )


def headline_metric(state):
    """Whichever metric has the stronger time-varying F2 score -- used to pick the chart."""
    wec, wnpv = f2_window(state, "matches_ec", "time_varying"), f2_window(state, "matches_npv", "time_varying")
    if wec is None:
        return "matches_npv"
    if wnpv is None:
        return "matches_ec"
    return "matches_ec" if wec["score"] >= wnpv["score"] else "matches_npv"

Supplementary context: party flips and margins¶

In [5]:
def last_flip_year(state, through_year=2024):
    """Most recent year the state's OWN popular-vote winner changed party."""
    sub = state_winner[(state_winner.state == state) & (state_winner.year <= through_year)].sort_values("year")
    parties, years = sub.state_party.tolist(), sub.year.tolist()
    for i in range(len(parties) - 1, 0, -1):
        if parties[i] != parties[i - 1]:
            return years[i]
    return None


def flips_in_window(state, y0, y1):
    """How many times the state's own winner changed party within [y0, y1]."""
    sub = state_winner[(state_winner.state == state) & (state_winner.year >= y0) & (state_winner.year <= y1)].sort_values("year")
    parties = sub.state_party.tolist()
    return sum(1 for a, b in zip(parties, parties[1:]) if a != b)


def margin_snapshot(state, years=(2016, 2020, 2024)):
    """Raw votes + margin vs. national margin for the most recent elections."""
    sub = margins[(margins.abbr == state) & (margins.year.isin(years))].sort_values("year")
    if sub.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame()
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "Year": sub.year.values,
        "D Votes": sub.D_votes.astype("Int64").values,
        "R Votes": sub.R_votes.astype("Int64").values,
        "Raw Margin (D-R)": (sub.D_votes - sub.R_votes).astype("Int64").values,
        "State Margin %": (sub.pres_margin * 100).round(1).values,
        "National Margin %": (sub.national_margin * 100).round(1).values,
        "Relative Margin %": (sub.relative_margin * 100).round(1).values,
    }).reset_index(drop=True)
In [6]:
def cusum_plot(state, metric=None, figsize=(8, 3.2)):
    """The F2 random walk: cumulative baseline-centered score over the state's
    full valid history, with the discovered best window shaded and its
    misses marked."""
    metric = metric or headline_metric(state)
    pairs = _valid_pairs(state, metric)
    w = f2_window(state, metric, "time_varying")
    years = [y for y, _ in pairs]

    running, cum = 0.0, []
    for y, b in pairs:
        running += (1 - YEARLY_P[metric][y]) if b else -YEARLY_P[metric][y]
        cum.append(running)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    # x-tick spacing of 20 years
    ax.set_xticks(range(min(years), max(years) + 1, 20))
    ax.set_xticklabels(range(min(years), max(years) + 1, 20), rotation=45)
    ax.axhline(0, color="gray", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--")
    ax.plot(years, cum, color=ACCENT, linewidth=1.6, marker="o", markersize=3)

    if w:
        ax.axvspan(w["start"] - 1, w["end"] + 1, color=HIGHLIGHT, alpha=0.15)
        # label the window start and end
        ax.text(w["start"], cum[years.index(w["start"])], f"{w['start']}", color=HIGHLIGHT, fontsize=8, ha="right", va="bottom")
        ax.text(w["end"], cum[years.index(w["end"])], f"{w['end']}", color=HIGHLIGHT, fontsize=8, ha="left", va="bottom")
        # label the missed years
        for my in w["miss_years"]:
            ax.plot(my, cum[years.index(my)], "o", color=MISS_COLOR, markersize=6, zorder=5)
            # place the year label far below
            ax.text(my, cum[years.index(my)] - 0.1 * max(cum), f"{my}", color=MISS_COLOR, fontsize=8, ha="center", va="bottom")

    ax.set_title(f"{state} \u2014 cumulative excess over baseline ({METRIC_LABEL[metric]})", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("Election year")
    ax.set_ylabel("Cumulative score")
    fig.tight_layout()
    return fig

State spotlight renderer¶

In [7]:
CATEGORY_LABEL = {
    "core": "Core \u2014 long-run F2-dominant bellwether",
    "used-to-be": "Used to be \u2014 historical bellwether, now gone",
    "modern-predictive": "Modern predictive state",
    "recent-drift": "Bellwether that drifted during the Bush era",
    "modern-bloc": "Current predictive bloc (\"Blue Wall\")",
    "honorable-mention": "Honorable mention \u2014 used to be swingy, locked in since 1992",
}

def render_spotlight(state, category=None):
    label = CATEGORY_LABEL.get(category, "")
    display(Markdown(f"### {state}" + (f"\n*{label}*" if label else "")))

    # F1 table
    f1_df = pd.DataFrame(
        [[METRIC_LABEL[m]] + f1_curve(state, m, kmax=3) for m in ["matches_ec", "matches_npv"]],
        columns=["Metric", "k=0", "k=1", "k=2", "k=3"],
    )
    display(Markdown("**F1 \u2014 longest streak tolerating *k* misses**"))
    display(f1_df)

    # F2 table
    f2_rows = []
    for m in ["matches_ec", "matches_npv"]:
        for b, blabel in [("pooled", "constant pooled"), ("time_varying", "time-varying")]:
            w = f2_window(state, m, b)
            if w is None:
                continue
            f2_rows.append([
                METRIC_LABEL[m], blabel, f"{w['start']}\u2013{w['end']}", w["length"],
                w["hits"], w["misses"], ", ".join(map(str, w["miss_years"])) or "\u2014", w["score"],
            ])
    f2_df = pd.DataFrame(f2_rows, columns=["Metric", "Baseline", "Window", "Length", "Hits", "Misses", "Miss Years", "Score"])
    display(Markdown("**F2 \u2014 baseline-centered best window (used for selection/ranking)**"))
    display(f2_df)

    # party context
    ctx_rows = []
    for m in ["matches_ec", "matches_npv"]:
        w = f2_window(state, m, "time_varying")
        if w is None:
            continue
        ctx_rows.append([METRIC_LABEL[m], f"{w['start']}\u2013{w['end']}", flips_in_window(state, w["start"], w["end"])])
    ctx_df = pd.DataFrame(ctx_rows, columns=["Metric", "F2 Window", "Party Flips Within Window"])
    lf = last_flip_year(state)
    display(Markdown(f"**Party context** \u2014 {state} last changed which party it voted for in **{lf}**."))
    display(ctx_df)

    # margin snapshot
    display(Markdown("**Recent margin snapshot**"))
    display(margin_snapshot(state))

    # chart
    cusum_plot(state, metric="matches_ec")
    cusum_plot(state, metric="matches_npv")
    plt.show()

Top States by F2 metric¶

In [8]:
CURATED = {
    "IL": "core", "OH": "core", "PA": "core", "NY": "core", "CA": "core", "MO": "core",
    "IN": "used-to-be",
    "NV": "modern-predictive", "NM": "modern-predictive",
    "TN": "recent-drift",
    "WI": "modern-bloc", "MI": "modern-bloc",
    "DE": "honorable-mention", "MD": "honorable-mention", "CT": "honorable-mention", "NJ": "honorable-mention",
}


def build_score_table():
    """Per-state table of all 4 F2 scores (metric x baseline), plus combos:
    *_robust = min(pooled, time_varying) for that metric -- discounts a score
    that only looks good under one baseline choice. headline = min(ec_robust,
    npv_robust) -- a state only ranks high here if EC and NPV both agree it's
    strong. specialist = max(ec_robust, npv_robust) -- the best single-axis
    case, tagged with which metric it leans on and how recent that window is,
    since a strong-but-stale run (e.g. ending decades ago) reads very
    differently from a strong-and-current one at the same score."""
    rows = []
    for state in sorted(statelevel.state.unique()):
        rec = {"state": state}
        for metric, mkey in [("matches_ec", "ec"), ("matches_npv", "npv")]:
            for baseline, bkey in [("pooled", "pool"), ("time_varying", "tv")]:
                w = f2_window(state, metric, baseline)
                rec[f"{mkey}_{bkey}"] = w["score"] if w else np.nan
                rec[f"{mkey}_{bkey}_end"] = w["end"] if w else np.nan
        rows.append(rec)
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("state")
    df["ec_robust"] = df[["ec_pool", "ec_tv"]].min(axis=1)
    df["npv_robust"] = df[["npv_pool", "npv_tv"]].min(axis=1)
    df["headline"] = df[["ec_robust", "npv_robust"]].min(axis=1)
    df["specialist"] = df[["ec_robust", "npv_robust"]].max(axis=1)
    df["specialist_metric"] = np.where(df["ec_robust"] >= df["npv_robust"], "EC", "NPV")
    df["specialist_end"] = np.where(
        df["specialist_metric"] == "EC",
        df[["ec_pool_end", "ec_tv_end"]].min(axis=1),
        df[["npv_pool_end", "npv_tv_end"]].min(axis=1),
    )
    return df


score_table = build_score_table()

# --- raw scores: where do the 4 individual rankings agree / disagree? ---
RAW_COLS = {
    "ec_pool": "EC × pooled", "ec_tv": "EC × time-varying",
    "npv_pool": "NPV × pooled", "npv_tv": "NPV × time-varying",
}
display(Markdown("### Top 12 by each raw score"))
for col, label in RAW_COLS.items():
    top = score_table[col].sort_values(ascending=False).head(12)
    display(Markdown(f"**{label}**"))
    display(pd.DataFrame({
        "Score": top.round(2).values,
        "Curated category": [CURATED.get(s, "—") for s in top.index],
    }, index=top.index))

# --- combined headline ranking: states where EC and NPV, pooled and time-varying, all agree ---
display(Markdown(
    "### Headline ranking — `min` across all 4 scores\n\n"
    "A state only scores well here if every metric × baseline combo agrees "
    "it's strong. This is what should recover the **core** / **modern-predictive** tier."
))
headline_view = score_table[["headline", "specialist", "specialist_metric", "specialist_end"]] \
    .sort_values("headline", ascending=False).round(2)
headline_view["Curated category"] = [CURATED.get(s, "—") for s in headline_view.index]
display(headline_view.head(18))

# --- specialists: states that lean hard on one metric, with how current that lean is ---
display(Markdown(
    "### Single-axis specialists (not already above) — `max` of the robust scores\n\n"
    "States that are strong on EC *or* NPV but not both. `specialist_end` is the "
    "last year in that metric's window — a specialist whose window is current "
    "(the last few cycles) reads very differently from one whose best run ended "
    "decades ago, even at a similar score. This is where **modern-bloc** and "
    "**honorable-mention** states should show up, alongside any un-curated "
    "states worth a second look."
))
already_shown = set(headline_view.head(18).index)
specialist_view = score_table.loc[~score_table.index.isin(already_shown)] \
    .sort_values("specialist", ascending=False)
specialist_view = specialist_view[["headline", "specialist", "specialist_metric", "specialist_end"]].round(2)
specialist_view["Curated category"] = [CURATED.get(s, "—") for s in specialist_view.index]
display(specialist_view.head(15))

Single-axis specialists (not already above) — max of the robust scores¶

States that are strong on EC or NPV but not both. specialist_end is the last year in that metric's window — a specialist whose window is current (the last few cycles) reads very differently from one whose best run ended decades ago, even at a similar score. This is where modern-bloc and honorable-mention states should show up, alongside any un-curated states worth a second look.
